note: Programs, engines and agents built to play games: board, card, video and quiz games, from 1950s machines to modern RL agents

aka: matchbox educable noughts and crosses engine
answers.q: 304 matchboxes of coloured beads that learned tic-tac-toe. Donald Michie, 1961.
Torres Quevedo's 1912 automaton, playing king and rook against a lone king.
A Nim-playing machine at the 1940 World's Fair. It won most of its games.
Noughts and crosses on Cambridge's EDSAC, 1952.
Tord Romstad's engine, forked into Stockfish in 2008.
Matthew Lai's 2015 chess engine that learned its evaluation by self-play. He then joined DeepMind.
Evolved, not programmed: a checkers net that reached expert level without human strategy.
Hans Berliner's backgammon program beat world champion Luigi Villa in 1979.
Essentially solved heads-up limit hold'em, 2015.
Expert-level Stratego, where the hidden pieces make bluffing part of the game.
Stripped of its world titles in 2011 after being ruled a derivative of Fruit and Crafty.
Deep Blue's CMU-born predecessor, named after the computer in The Hitchhiker's Guide.
Turing and Champernowne's 1948 chess program, run by hand because no computer could yet.
Beat Othello world champion Takeshi Murakami 6–0 in 1997.
DreamerV3 collected Minecraft diamonds from scratch, no human data.
Remember promising states, return to them, then explore. Montezuma's Revenge finally fell.
Sony AI's Gran Turismo racer that beat top human drivers, with sportsmanship in the reward.
Learned Minecraft from 70,000 hours of YouTube, then crafted a diamond pickaxe.
GPT-4 playing Minecraft by writing its own library of code skills.
SethBling's NEAT-evolved network clearing a Super Mario World level, 2015.
Claude grinding through Pokémon Red on a Twitch stream, 2025. Mt. Moon was a struggle.
Learned Go from self-play alone and beat the version that beat Lee Sedol 100–0.
Beat Dota 2 world champions OG in April 2019.
Grandmaster level in StarCraft II with all three races, 2019.
Beat four top heads-up no-limit pros over 120,000 hands, 2017.
Beat elite pros at six-player no-limit hold'em. Training cost: about $150 of cloud compute.
Beat Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter in 2011. Once answered a US Cities clue with "What is Toronto?????"
Volunteer-trained, open-source AlphaZero for chess.
Human-level Diplomacy: it had to negotiate, persuade and mostly keep its promises.
One network, raw pixels, 49 Atari games. Nature, 2015.
First agent to beat the human baseline on all 57 Atari games.
Solved checkers in 2007: perfect play from both sides is a draw.
Arthur Samuel's self-improving checkers player, the 1959 paper that named machine learning.
AlphaZero without being told the rules: it learns its own model of the game.
Tesauro's 1992 self-taught backgammon net. It changed how the pros play their openings.
Beat Lee Sedol 4–1 in 2016. Move 37 still gets talked about.
Taught itself chess, shogi and Go from the rules alone, then crushed Stockfish.
Beat Kasparov in 1997 with 480 custom chess chips and brute-force search.
